subject: Acme POC: evaluation plan and success criteria
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Claire Nguyen <claire.nguyen@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 14:10:00 -0000
Subject: Discovery follow-up — next steps for POC

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the call earlier — gave a solid sense of Redwood's serving and routing features. Claire and I discussed internally and we're excited to move to a short POC to validate latency/cost and end-to-end quality on our agent summarization workload.

A few quick things we care about for the POC:
- Success criteria: 95th pctile latency < 300ms on 256-token outputs; cost <= $0.002 per 1k tokens; ROUGE-L >= baseline by 2 points on our eval set.
- Eval scope: ~10k sample requests (mix of short/long), production-like prompt templates, and user-safety regression checks.
- Timeline: 4-week trial preferred.

Can Redwood propose an evaluation plan, ownership, and a concrete kickoff date? Also loops: we'll need a technical contact on both sides for infra/setup.

Thanks,
Samir
Principal Product Manager — Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@acme.com>
Cc: Claire Nguyen <claire.nguyen@acme.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 18:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up — next steps for POC

Hi Samir / Claire — great to meet you both earlier. Appreciate the clear success criteria. I've put together a recommended POC/eval approach and pulled in Dylan (solutions engineer) + Rachel (eval lead) to own setup and grading. High-level proposal below; happy to iterate.

POC summary (4 weeks)
- Week 0 (kickoff): align goals, exchange access & data sample, confirm metrics and evaluation dataset.
- Week 1: infra setup, model variants + quantization profiles deployed in test env, streaming/timeout configs tuned.
- Week 2: run offline evals (10k samples) + initial regression checks.
- Week 3: online shadowing of real traffic (48–72h windows) + manual QA on edge cases.
- Week 4: results review, final tweaks, and a decision meeting.

Success criteria (proposed)
- Latency: 95th percentile for 256-token outputs < 300ms (test harness).
- Cost: projected token cost <= $0.002 per 1k tokens, assuming baseline batching.
- Quality: ROUGE-L increase >= 2 points on Acme's eval set OR human-rated usefulness score >= 4/5 on a 200-sample set.

Evaluation methodology
- Offline evals: run the curated 10k sample set across model variants. Compute ROUGE / BLEU / embedding-similarity and run safety/regression checks.
- Online shadow: route a fraction of traffic in non-productive mode to measure real-latency, end-to-end integration, and failure modes.
- Grading rubric: automated metrics + sampled human grading for domain-specific correctness. Rachel, see the attached rubric and can you confirm the grading buckets and thresholds?

Owners
- Redwood PM / AE: Marissa Cole (overall POC owner / commercial).
- Solutions engineer: Dylan Brooks (env, model tuning, infra).
- Eval lead (Redwood): Rachel Kim (offline test harness, grading, final report).
- Acme technical lead: Samir Shah (data access, workload definitions).

Next steps
1) Claire/Samir: confirm timeline and any non-negotiable data/privacy constraints.
2) Redwood: schedule kickoff — propose Mon, Jun 28th 10:00am PT or Tue, Jun 29th 9:00am PT.
3) Exchange sample dataset (S3 link or secure upload) and account permissions.

Attachments: Acme-POC-MAP-v1.pdf (POC milestone map), poc-eval-rubric.xlsx (draft rubric).

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Samir Shah <samir.shah@acme.com>
Cc: Claire Nguyen <claire.nguyen@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 07:15:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up — next steps for POC (eval rubric draft)

Hi all — attaching a more explicit eval methodology and grading rubric (eval-methodology-v2.docx). Key points: 

1) Offline vs online:
- Offline (10k samples): automated metrics (ROUGE-L, BLEU, cosine sim on embeddings) + safety/regression checks. Use automated pass/fail thresholds where possible to give fast feedback.
- Online shadow: measure real-world latency, error rates, and real prompt distribution differences. Use a sampled set (n=500) for human rating against domain-specific correctness.

2) Grading rubric (proposed buckets):
- Automated pass: meets both latency and cost projection AND automated quality thresholds.
- Human-sampled pass: >=80% of sampled responses rated >=4/5 on relevance/usefulness and no critical safety regressions.
- Final pass: both automated pass and human-sampled pass.

3) Disagreements & tie-breakers:
- If automated metrics and human samples disagree, we'll run a focused adjudication set (200 additional samples) and escalate to a joint review.

4) Reporting deliverables:
- Week 2: Offline metrics + initial flag list for regressions.
- Week 3: Shadow results + sampled human ratings.
- Week 4: Final report with recommended config (model variant + batching) and projected monthly unit-cost.

Samir — two quick questions for alignment: (a) do you have internal reviewers for the human sample set (we recommend 3 domain SMEs), and (b) any PII or redaction needs for the sample payloads?

Thanks,
Rachel
Research & Evals — Redwood Inference
